_about: How the lenses resolve a stored name to the addresses it reaches. A name's DNS relations (purpose dns in the semantics table) lead to an address when the other end is one of address_types, and to another name when the record type is one of alias_rr_types: a CNAME makes its owner an alias of the target, whose records apply instead (RFC 1034 section 3.6.2). delegation_rr_types are the records that delegate a zone to name servers (NS, RFC 1034 section 4.2.1). mail_rr_types are the records naming a domain's mail servers (MX, RFC 5321 section 5.1). max_alias_depth bounds an alias chain; resolvers bound them too, since a chain can loop (RFC 1034 section 5.3.2). record_type_names maps a stored record's numeric RR type to the label the lenses show; a type absent from the map is shown as TYPE<number>. name_server_providers name the managed-DNS providers whose authoritative name servers serve many unrelated customers, so that a name server matching one is not read as evidence of shared ownership by the shared-name-server horizontal signal (the mail-exchanger equivalent is email.json mail_providers): pattern is a regular expression matched, ignoring case, against the whole name server host name, and source is the provider's own documentation of the host names it assigns. This recognizes a provider regardless of how many of its customers are in the database, where the apex-count cap only catches it once many are. A name server no pattern matches is still subject to that cap. Add providers here, not in Go code, and only with such a source. Add values here, not in Go code.
